chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'When Arafaat is constricted, what do they do?' He said, 'They ascend to the mountain.'

key_terms.الْجَبَلِ: The mountain, referring to the hills surrounding Arafat
key_terms.ضَاقَتْ: Constricted, crowded, or limited in space
key_terms.عَرَفَةُ: Arafat, the sacred plain where the central ritual of Hajj takes place

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if Arafat is too crowded during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of ascending the surrounding mountains, such as Jabal al-Rahmah, to fulfill the ritual standing (wuquf) at Arafat when the main plain is overcrowded. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of the Hajj rites, ensuring the obligation is met even under conditions of physical constraint, while maintaining the sanctity of the station.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Sama’at who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘When there is constriction at Arafaat, what should we be doing?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be going higher to the mountain’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘What should people do if ‘Arafat becomes full?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘They can go higher toward the hills.’” NOTE: (Fatwa best explains Hadith 11 of this Chapter)
